recognize_zh: 周邊血抹片可見多顆碎裂紅血球（schistocytes），包括頭盔狀（helmet cell）、三角形與不規則碎片，並有少數小球形紅血球，血小板稀少，符合微血管病變性溶血（此例為非典型 HUS）。
features: Numerous schistocytes including helmet cells, triangular and irregular fragments
Normocytic red cell background with mild anisocytosis
Markedly reduced platelets, with only rare small platelets in the field
Single small lymphocyte; no nucleated red cells or blasts seen
describe_en: Peripheral blood smear shows numerous schistocytes, including helmet cells, triangular forms and irregular red cell fragments, with occasional microspherocytes. Platelets are markedly decreased, with only rare forms seen in this field. White cells in the field are unremarkable, and no leukemic cells are identified. Findings are consistent with a microangiopathic hemolytic anemia with thrombocytopenia; in a child with acute renal failure, no diarrheal prodrome and anti-complement factor H antibodies, this supports atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome.

ddx.vs: TTP shows an identical schistocytic smear, so it is separated by severely deficient ADAMTS13 activity (below 10%) rather than morphology.
STEC-HUS has the same smear but follows bloody diarrhea with stool Shiga toxin or E. coli O157 positivity, unlike complement-mediated aHUS.
DIC can show schistocytes but has prolonged PT/aPTT with low fibrinogen and high D-dimer, whereas coagulation tests are typically normal in aHUS.
Valve-related hemolysis shows schistocytes with normal platelet counts and no renal thrombotic microangiopathy.
